circum-verto or circum verto (-vorto ), ĕre, v. a.,
I.to turn around (rare; “not in Cic.): citius quam rotula circumvortitur,” Plaut. Pers. 3, 3, 39 ; cf.: rota circumvertitur axem, turns or is turned around on its axis, Ov. M. 15, 522 (Merkel, circumvolvitur): “ubi circumvortor, cado,” turn myself around, Plaut. Ps. 5, 1, 32 ; cf.: circumvertens se, turning one's self to the right side, * Suet. Vit. 2; “v. the commentt. in h. l.: mancipium,” to declare free, Quint. Decl. 342 ; v. circumago, I. B. (in Plaut. Ps. 1, 5, 127, perh. a false reading for intervortant, which Fleck. adopts; cf. Lorenz ad loc.).
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
